one_month_reasoning: No earnings in the window: Q2 FY27 was reported 2026-09-02 and Q3 FY27 should land around late Nov/early Dec, after 2026-10-30. In-window items are minor: the company's motion to dismiss the securities class action is due 2026-10-13 (a filing, not a ruling); the $3.75B zero-coupon convertible (priced 2026-09-28, conversion prices ~$484/$500, capped calls to $820) is done, so convert-arb short hedging pressure that knocked the stock ~4% should be mostly spent; a Form 144 insider sale notice (2026-09-27) adds modest supply. Post-earnings drift from the +20% Sep-2 gap has already fully reversed (380 -> ~330s), so no drift edge either way. Hyperscaler earnings in late October (cloud consumption read-through) are the main macro swing factor. With no directional edge I centre the distribution on spot $337.50 with ~16% monthly vol (between realized 62%/3.5 = 17.7% and a lower forward vol after the April tariff crash drops out).

fair_value.method: Blend of EV/NTM sales (13x ~$9.4B NTM revenue at Sep-2027 -> ~$322), SBC-aware FCF multiple (45x ~$2.45B NTM adj. FCF -> ~$290) and forward P/E (85x ~$3.70 NTM non-GAAP EPS -> ~$315), plus ~$1.7B net cash, on ~385M diluted shares; blended ~$310, slightly below spot.

bear.story: Consumption slows as AI-driven efficiency and Iceberg/open formats reduce storage/compute lock-in, Databricks SQL (>$1B run-rate, >100% growth) takes warehouse share, product growth decelerates toward ~20% by FY28, and the software multiple compresses to ~9-10x NTM sales. SBC dilution and a possible 2027 Databricks IPO providing a cheaper-growth alternative weigh further.

base.story: Growth decelerates from 37% to high-20s as comps harden; margins expand ~2-3 pts; multiple compresses ~20% from ~17x to ~13-14x NTM sales, roughly offsetting ~25-30% revenue growth, leaving the stock near current levels.

bull.story: AI workloads (Cortex, agents, coding) keep product growth in the mid-30s through FY28, NRR climbs past 128%, operating margin guidance steps up, and the multiple holds ~17x; stock approaches the convert conversion prices (~$484-$500) and top sell-side targets ($500-525).

thesis_break_reason: Below ~$220 (about -35%, ~9x NTM sales) the market would be pricing growth falling to ~20% or lower with NRR sliding toward 115%, i.e. the post-Q2 reacceleration was a one-off. That is a fundamental break rather than ordinary 60%-vol noise, though note the stock already visited $118 in the April 2026 tariff crash, so a macro liquidation can reach this level without a fundamental cause.

reasoning: Starting point: SNOW at $337.50 after a violent year (April tariff crash to $118, then Q1 and Q2 beats; Q2 FY27 product revenue +37% with FY27 guide raised to $6.07B/+36%, op margin 14.5%, adj FCF margin 23%, RPO $9.0B +30%, NRR 126%). The stock gapped to ~$380 on Sep 3 and has since given back the entire gap, partly on a $3.75B zero-coupon convert (priced Sep 28) and a Form 144 insider sale notice. Skeptic lane findings: (1) valuation is the core bear point: ~17x NTM sales, ~100x forward non-GAAP EPS, GAAP loss-making with SBC ~30% of revenue and ~$1B of insider selling over the past year; (2) short interest ~5.7% of float, ~$6B notional, near highs; (3) securities class action alleging efficiency gains/Iceberg/tiered storage would hurt consumption is past the amended complaint stage with MTD due Oct 13; the 2024 data-breach MDL has produced only small settlements so far; (4) Databricks is growing 65-80% at a $5-7B run-rate, with its SQL warehouse >$1B and growing >100%, which is the most credible long-run share threat; (5) credit is not a concern: net cash ~$1.7B, the new convert carries a 0% coupon and 47-52% premium, which is a vote of confidence from convert buyers rather than distress. Weighing honestly: the fundamentals just reaccelerated and 43 of 50 analysts are Buy (avg target ~$414-425), so the bear case rests on multiple compression rather than a broken business. My SBC-aware blended fair value is ~$310 (EV/sales 13x, FCF 45x, P/E 85x) versus consensus targets ~$415; I set the 12-month median at roughly spot (~$335-340) because growth of ~25-30% offsets expected multiple compression, and I use a wide distribution (~45-50% effective vol, below the 62% realized that includes the tariff crash) with a modestly fat left tail. Scenario mean (~$345) is near the ladder's implied mean. One-month: no earnings in window; neutral, centred on spot. Research limits: SEC.gov direct downloads were rate-limited (used WebFetch of the 8-K instead), Twelve Data/Alpha Vantage estimate endpoints were unavailable, Seeking Alpha downgrade article was paywalled (403); no X/prediction-market data was used.
